score_reasons.quality: Cinematic rendering is clean: Tang-dynasty gate architecture, banners and ranks of armored soldiers read clearly; foreground figures are silhouetted so no anatomy failures; slight banner-cloth deformation and overall softness are the only blemishes.
score_reasons.aesthetics: Strong poster composition with unified golden-sepia palette, atmospheric haze and backlit sun, clear three-tier hierarchy of title, subtitle and scene; mood of tension before the ambush is well conveyed.
score_reasons.alignment: Only the text layer matches the brief. The essential creative premise — a WeChat Moments (朋友圈) interface for the Xuanwu Gate Incident — is entirely absent: no phone UI, feed, avatars, likes or comments anywhere. What is delivered is a conventional historical event illustration. The short date line is garbled pseudo-text. Main title and subtitle are correct and the no-micro-print constraint is respected.
score_reasons.real_world_fidelity: Tang-style gate towers, city walls, period armor and banners are plausible for 626 CE with no visible anachronisms or cultural errors; nothing offensive or non-compliant.
score_reasons.creative_generation: The mashup concept (ancient coup retold as social-media feed) was not executed at all; as a standalone historical poster it is competent but conventional, so imaginative fusion and information layering score low.
